docs.doc: Defines TelegramBotService, AuthenticationModule, MessageHandler, BackendClient, and StreamingHandler components with responsibilities, inputs, and outputs. Includes complete data models for User Message, Backend API Request/Response, and SSE Stream events.
First token latency for thinking models: 10-30 seconds with "Annie is thinking" indicators. Message receipt: <1s, Authorization check: <50ms, Backend API call: <10s timeout.

User authorization via AUTHORIZED_USER_IDS whitelist (comma-separated Telegram user IDs). Authorization check BEFORE backend forwarding (fail-fast pattern). Unauthorized attempts logged for security monitoring.
Message Processing Sequence: Telegram polling → message extract → authorization check → (if unauthorized: rejection, STOP) → (if authorized: typing indicator → backend forwarding → stream handling).

Users want AI-powered decision support via Telegram bot with streaming responses, memory integration, and real-time information access. Target: help with 80% of day-to-day decisions with 80% user trust.

Telegram Bot Service uses python-telegram-bot library, polls Telegram API, forwards messages to Backend API via HTTP, streams responses to users. Features: Long polling (V1), message splitting, error handling, retries.
Required environment variables: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, AUTHORIZED_USER_IDS (comma-separated user IDs), BACKEND_URL (default: http://backend:8000), LOG_LEVEL, ENVIRONMENT.
Service dependencies: redis → mcp-server → backend → telegram-bot. All services have health checks and restart policies (unless-stopped).

constraints.constraint: Telegram bot operates as isolated Docker container within annie-network, communicating exclusively with Backend API via HTTP. No direct access to Redis, MCP server, or LLM APIs.
Service communication flow: Telegram API → Long Polling → Telegram Bot → HTTP POST /api/chat → Backend API. Streaming handled in Story 5.2.
User authorization via AUTHORIZED_USER_IDS whitelist MUST occur BEFORE backend forwarding (fail-fast pattern). Authorization check target: <50ms.

Unauthorized users receive rejection message: "Sorry, you're not authorized to use Annie. Please contact the administrator for access." Unauthorized attempts logged with user_id for security monitoring.
Message receipt latency: <1 second from Telegram API to bot processing. Backend API call timeout: 10 seconds. Long polling timeout: 30 seconds.
Structured logging with JSON format (production). Required signals: message_received, authorization, backend_call, unauthorized_attempt. Mask sensitive data (message content, PII).
Retry logic with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, max 3 retries). Graceful degradation when backend unavailable. User-friendly error messages (no technical jargon).
Long polling timeout: 30 seconds maximum. Rate limiting: 30 messages/second per bot. Message length limit: 4096 characters (Story 5.2 concern).
Use async/await patterns from Story 3.2 for HTTP client. Use aiohttp for backend communication (same as MemoryClient). Apply structured logging pattern with user context.
Follow graceful degradation patterns: continue core functionality when external services fail, return user-friendly error messages, log failures but don't crash.
Test thoroughly - don't defer testing. Use pytest-asyncio for async tests, respx for mocking httpx/aiohttp. Target: >80% code coverage.

interface.name: POST /api/chat
interface.description: Backend endpoint for submitting user messages for processing. Telegram bot forwards authorized messages here.

interface.name: GET /api/stream/{conversation_id}
interface.signature: GET /api/stream/{conversation_id} Response: SSE event stream Event Types: - {"type": "token", "content": "text"} // Incremental text - {"type": "done", "tokens_used": {...}} // Completion - {"type": "error", "message": "..."} // Failure Errors: 404 (conversation not found), 500 (streaming error)
interface.description: SSE streaming endpoint for LLM responses. Story 5.2 will implement streaming handler to consume this.

interface.name: GET /health
interface.description: Backend health check endpoint for verifying availability before forwarding messages.

interface.name: python-telegram-bot Application
interface.signature:
from telegram.ext import Application, ApplicationBuilder, MessageHandler, filters
app = ApplicationBuilder().token(bot_token).build() app.add_handler(MessageHandler(filters.TEXT, handle_message)) await app.run_polling(allowed_updates=["message"], timeout=30)
interface.description: python-telegram-bot 20.7 async API for bot initialization, handler registration, and long polling.

interface.name: Telegram Update Object
interface.signature: update.message.from_user.id // Telegram user ID (int) update.message.chat_id // Telegram chat ID (int) update.message.text // Message text (str) update.message.message_id // Message ID (int) update.message.date // Timestamp (datetime) update.message.from_user.username // Username (str | None) update.message.voice // Voice message object (if voice)
interface.description: Telegram Update object structure for extracting message data in message handlers.

interface.name: aiohttp.ClientSession
interface.signature:
import aiohttp
async with aiohttp.ClientSession(timeout=timeout) as session: async with session.post(url, json=payload) as response: response.raise_for_status() return await response.json()
interface.description: aiohttp async HTTP client pattern for backend API communication. Follow MemoryClient patterns from Story 3.1.

tests.standards: Follow testing patterns from Story 3.2: Use pytest-asyncio for async tests, respx for mocking aiohttp requests, AsyncMock for mocking async methods. Test both success and failure paths. Target >80% code coverage. Unit tests should be fast (<1s per test) and deterministic with all external services mocked. Integration tests use mocked backend API or Docker backend. Performance tests validate latency targets (<1s message receipt, <50ms auth check).

idea.description: Test bot connects to Telegram API successfully - mock telegram.ext.Application.run_polling, verify called with correct parameters (allowed_updates, timeout)
Test AuthenticationModule.load_whitelist - valid comma-separated user IDs loaded into set, invalid IDs logged as errors, verify <50ms lookup performance with timeit
Test authorized user message processing - mock telegram Update with authorized user_id, verify message handled within 1s, backend client called
Test unauthorized user rejection - mock Update with unauthorized user_id, verify rejection message sent via reply_text, backend NOT called, attempt logged
Test message data extraction - mock Update, verify user_id, message_text, timestamp, message_id extracted correctly, structured log entry contains all fields
Test text message handling - mock Update with text message, authorized user, verify handle_message called, typing indicator sent, backend forwarding triggered
Test voice message handling - mock Update with voice message, verify 'Voice messages coming soon' reply sent, voice duration logged
Test backend API forwarding - mock BackendClient.send_message, verify POST /api/chat called with correct payload (user_id prefixed 'telegram_', platform, message, conversation_id)
Test connection failure retry - mock backend connection error, verify retry logic with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s), max 3 attempts, user error message on final failure
Test unauthorized attempt logging - mock unauthorized user_id, verify log entry contains user_id, authorized:false, no message content (privacy), event:unauthorized_attempt
Integration test: Full message flow - authorized user → message handler → authorization check → backend forwarding → response, verify end-to-end latency <1s
Integration test: Backend unavailable - stop backend, send message, verify graceful degradation, user-friendly error, logs backend failure
Performance test: Authorization check latency - measure is_authorized with 100 users in whitelist, verify <50ms p95
Security test: SQL injection in user message - send message with SQL injection patterns, verify sanitized before backend forwarding, no errors
